# search


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) asks
several search engines the same question at once and merges their
answers into one list. Asking several engines helps because each one
misses pages the others find, and a page that several engines rank
highly is usually a good one. The engines are reached through
[ddgs](https://github.com/deedy5/ddgs), which needs no API keys. The
lists are merged with reciprocal rank fusion, explained below, and can
then be reordered by how well each result matches the query.

[`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)
gets Google’s own ranking by loading the results page in a stealth
browser, which is slower.
[`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)
goes a step further than either: it searches, downloads the best results
that have readable text, and returns them as one markdown digest that
cites each source, ready to hand to a language model.

## The ddgs client

[`get_ddgs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#get_ddgs)
returns one shared `DDGS` client, created on first use.
[`ddgs_env`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#ddgs_env)
reads proxy and certificate settings from the environment so that search
works behind a corporate proxy: the proxy from `DDGS_PROXY`,
`HTTPS_PROXY` or `https_proxy`, and a certificate bundle from
`FOSSICK_CA_BUNDLE`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` or
`CURL_CA_BUNDLE`.

## Asking each engine

For text search, fossick queries each engine in `TEXT_BACKENDS`
separately and keeps each engine’s results in the order that engine
ranked them. It does not use ddgs’s own combined search, which picks
engines at random and favours Wikipedia.
[`backends`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#backends)
lists every engine ddgs offers for a category. With `pages` above 1,
fossick asks each engine for that many pages of results, and drops
results on later pages that repeat earlier ones. The test below checks
that the ranks keep counting across pages.

## Merging the lists

Reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) merges ranked lists without needing the
engines’ own scores, which are not comparable. Each page gets
`1/(k + rank)` from every list it appears in, and those amounts are
added up. A page ranked first by one engine scores more than a page
ranked eighth, and a page found by several engines adds up a score from
each. `k`, 60 by default, controls how much more the top ranks count
than the lower ones.

[`rrf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#rrf) treats
two URLs as the same page when they differ only in scheme, `www.`, a
trailing slash or tracking parameters, using
[`norm_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#norm_url)
from `fossick.quality`. For each page it keeps the longest snippet any
engine gave, the fused `score`, and `engines`, the list of engines that
found it.

## Reranking

Search engines rank by many things besides relevance to the exact words
asked.
[`rerank`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#rerank)
reorders results by how well their title, snippet and URL match the
query, and blends that with the merged score. `mix` is the weight given
to the merged score, 0.4 by default; at 1 the reranker is ignored. Each
result gains a
[`rerank`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#rerank)
field holding its relevance score.

`method` chooses the scorer. `'lexical'` uses BM25, a standard
word-matching formula, computed with
[`bm25`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#bm25) over
the results themselves, so no index is needed. `'flashrank'` uses
[flashrank](https://github.com/PrithivirajDamodaran/FlashRank)’s small
cross-encoder model, which reads the query and each result together and
is better at matching meaning; it needs `pip install flashrank`, and
[`flashrank_scores`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#flashrank_scores)
returns None when it is missing. `'auto'` uses flashrank when installed
and BM25 otherwise. `'none'`, the default for
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search), keeps
the merged order.

## Where and when

The best answer to many questions depends on the country: building
rules, prices and what is for sale all differ. Search engines take a
region code of the form `country-language`, such as `au-en`. With
`region='auto'`, the default, fossick works the two halves out
separately from the query.

[`infer_country`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#infer_country)
looks for country names, adjectives and big cities from `COUNTRY_WORDS`,
and answers only when exactly one country is named; a query comparing
two countries gets None.
[`infer_language`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#infer_language)
counts common function words from `LANG_WORDS`, such as “the” and “what”
or “der” and “und”, and answers only when one language clearly leads
with at least two matches.
[`infer_region`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#infer_region)
joins them. A query that names no language takes the usual language of
the country it names, from `COUNTRY_LANG`, and whatever the query leaves
open comes from the default, `us-en`. So an English question about
France gives `fr-en`: French sources, in English where possible.

`timelimit` keeps only recent results: `'d'`, `'w'`, `'m'` or `'y'` for
the past day, week, month or year.

## [`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search)

[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) is the
main entry point. For text it queries every engine in `TEXT_BACKENDS` in
parallel, merges the lists with RRF and reranks them with `method`;
`backend='google'` restricts it to one engine. The number of engines
asked does not depend on `n`, which only cuts the final list; raise
`pages` when you want more candidates to choose from. With `fuse=False`,
or for the
[`images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#images),
[`news`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#news) and
`books` categories, it uses ddgs’s own search for that category. The
[`videos`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#videos)
category searches YouTube with
[`search_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search_yt).

An empty query returns an empty list without touching the network. When
every engine fails,
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) prints
one warning and returns an empty list. `text`,
[`images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#images),
[`news`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#news),
[`videos`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#videos) and
`books` are
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) with
the category already set, and
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#extract)
downloads one URL with ddgs and returns its content, as markdown by
default.

## [`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)

[`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)
loads Google’s results page in the stealth browser and reads the results
off it, so the ranking is Google’s own. It is slower than
[`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search) and
needs scrapling’s browsers. It takes the same `region` and `timelimit`
as [`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search):
the country biases the ranking without excluding other countries, and
the time limit uses Google’s own filter. Its results have the same shape
as [`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search)’s,
with the snippet under `content`. If Google returns nothing or the
browser fails, it returns an empty list and prints a warning.

## [`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)

[`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)
turns a question into a set of readable sources. It goes through these
steps:

1.  [`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan),
    from `fossick.quality`, splits a question that asks several things
    into one search per part, and keeps the original question as the
    first search.
2.  Each search runs with
    [`search`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search),
    or with
    [`google`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#google)
    when `engine='google'`. Their results are interleaved, taking one
    from each in turn, so that each part of the question gets sources.
3.  With `curated=True`, the default,
    [`curate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#curate)
    removes sites that copy other sites’ content and moves authoritative
    sources up. Copycats are dropped before any page is downloaded.
4.  It downloads the candidates in order, `n` at a time, with
    `fetch(auto=True)`, until it has `n` pages with at least 400
    characters of readable markdown. A page that failed, was blocked, or
    was too short goes into `dropped` with its reason, and the next
    candidate takes its place.
5.  With `focused=True`,
    [`focus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#focus)
    cuts each page down to about `chars` characters of the passages that
    best answer the question.

It returns a dictionary with the `query`, the `sources`, the `digest`,
the `dropped` pages, the `region` it used, the `curation` report and the
[`plan`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/quality.html#plan). Each
source holds its `title`, `href`, the fetch `tier` that worked, its
publication `date`, the `queries` it answered and its markdown in `md`.
The digest joins the sources, separated by `---`, each headed by its
title, URL, publication date when known, and the part of the question it
answers.

Three helpers are useful on their own.
[`page_date`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#page_date)
finds the date a page says it was published, from its JSON-LD data, its
`<meta>` tags (the names in `DATE_META`), a `<time>` element, or a
`/2018/09/` style URL, and returns it as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or None.
[`usable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#usable)
checks that a fetched page is a real 200 response, not a bot wall, and
has at least `min_chars` characters of readable markdown; `min_chars=0`
skips the length check.
[`focus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#focus) keeps
the parts of a long page that answer a query: it keeps the opening
blocks up to 30% of the budget, because reference pages often answer in
their first paragraphs, then adds the blocks that score best for the
query, and returns them in their original order with `…` marking the
gaps.

The cell below this one tests paging with stand-in engines.

``` python
# pagination: ranks run on across pages, and page 2's repeats of page 1 don't get counted twice
_seen = []
def _fake(be, q, region='us-en', page=1, timeout=8, tries=2, **kw):
    _seen.append((be, page))
    start = (page-1)*2
    return [dict(title=f'{be}{i}', href=f'https://e.com/{be}/{i}', body='', engine=be, rank=i-start+1)
            for i in range(start, start+3)]        # 3 hits/page, overlapping the next page by one
_real, _engine_hits = _engine_hits, _fake
try:
    one = _backend_lists('q', ('brave',), pages=1)
    two = _backend_lists('q', ('brave',), pages=2)
finally: _engine_hits = _real

assert sorted(_seen) == [('brave',1), ('brave',1), ('brave',2)], _seen   # one job per (backend, page)
assert len(one[0]) == 3 and len(two[0]) == 5                             # 3+3 minus the one repeat
assert [h['rank'] for h in two[0]] == [1,2,3,4,5]                        # continuous, not 1,2,3,1,2,3
assert len({h['href'] for h in two[0]}) == 5                             # deduped within the backend
```

### research

``` python
def research(
    q:str, # search query
    n:int=5, # number of readable sources to gather
    engine:str='search', # 'search' (fused metasearch) or 'google' (stealth browser ranking)
    sel:str=None, # CSS selector to narrow each page before markdown
    chars:int=4000, # max markdown chars kept per page
    auto:bool=True, # auto-escalate fetching (plain->heavy->stealthy->session) per page
    region:str='auto', # ddgs region, or 'auto' to read the country off the query
    timelimit:str=None, # d | w | m | y — only sources from the last day/week/month/year
    curated:bool=True, # drop mirror domains and rank by source authority before reading
    intent:str='auto', # authority class ('policy', 'docs', …), 'auto' to read it off `q`
    facets:int=4, # searches to fan out over when `q` holds more than one question; 1 disables
    rewrite:NoneType=None, # optional `f(q) -> list[str]` (a model) in place of the heuristic planner
    focused:bool=True, # keep query-relevant passages instead of the first `chars` chars
    candidates:int=None, # how many hits to draw on when backfilling (default 3n)
    pages:int=1, # result pages per backend (raise it when `candidates` exceeds one page)
    concurrency:int=8, **kw
)->dict: # extra kwargs passed to fetch()
```

*Search for `q`, read the top `n` readable results, and return them with
a markdown digest that cites each one.*

## Tests

The first cells run offline: they test empty queries, the Google results
parser, URL normalisation and RRF, BM25 and
[`focus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#focus), bot
wall detection, region inference, that `region` and `timelimit` reach
every engine,
[`page_date`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/search.html#page_date),
and the shape of
[`research`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#research)’s
result. The cells after them run real searches and are skipped by the
tests; their saved output shows what each call returns.

``` python
# empty query is a no-op for every entry point (no network)
assert search('') == []
assert research('')['sources'] == []
assert rrf([]) == [] and rerank('x', []) == []

# Google SERP parser works on a static fixture (no browser/network)
_serp = ('<html><body><div class="MjjYud"><div class="g">'
         '<a href="https://ex.com/p"><h3>Example Page</h3></a>'
         '<div class="VwiC3b">A short snippet.</div></div></div>'
         '<div><a href="https://www.google.com/aclk"><h3>Ad</h3></a></div></body></html>')
_g = _parse_google(_serp, 5)
assert len(_g) == 1, f'expected 1 organic result, got {len(_g)}'   # google.com ad link filtered out
assert _g[0]['href'] == 'https://ex.com/p' and _g[0]['title'] == 'Example Page'
assert _g[0]['content'] == 'A short snippet.'
```

``` python
# urls that differ only by scheme/www/trailing slash/tracking params are one page
assert norm_url('https://www.x.com/a/?utm_source=t#frag') == norm_url('http://x.com/a')
assert norm_url('https://x.com/a') != norm_url('https://x.com/b')

_g = [dict(href='https://x.com/1', rank=1, engine='google'), dict(href='https://x.com/8', rank=8, engine='google')]
_b = [dict(href='https://x.com/8', rank=8, engine='brave'),  dict(href='https://x.com/2', rank=2, engine='brave')]

# two urls, one backend each: the better-ranked one wins. ddgs ties them and orders by thread completion.
_solo = rrf([_g[:1], _b[1:]])
assert [h['href'] for h in _solo] == ['https://x.com/1', 'https://x.com/2'], _solo

# agreement across backends still outranks a single strong hit — that part of ddgs' instinct is right
_f = rrf([_g, _b])
assert _f[0]['href'] == 'https://x.com/8' and _f[0]['engines'] == ['google', 'brave']
assert len(_f) == 3                                                    # deduped across backends

# nothing is hoisted by domain: wikipedia earns its place from rank like everything else
_w = rrf([[dict(href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust', rank=7, engine='google'),
           dict(href='https://actix.rs/', rank=1, engine='google')]])
assert _w[0]['href'] == 'https://actix.rs/', _w
```

``` python
# BM25 ranks the doc that actually covers the query terms
_docs = ['sqlite wal mode benchmark write ahead log', 'a recipe for banana bread', 'wal mode']
_s = bm25('sqlite wal mode benchmark', _docs)
assert _s[0] == max(_s) and _s[1] == 0.0, _s

# rerank pulls the on-topic hit up past a higher-retrieval-score off-topic one
_hits = [dict(href='https://a.com/cake', title='Banana bread', body='baking', score=1.0),
         dict(href='https://b.com/sqlite-wal-benchmark', title='SQLite WAL benchmark', body='wal vs journal', score=0.9)]
assert rerank('sqlite wal benchmark', _hits, method='lexical')[0]['href'].startswith('https://b.com')

# focus() keeps the passage that answers the query, not the first N chars
_md = ('Cookie notice. We use cookies.\n\n' + 'Navigation menu home about contact.\n\n'*8 +
       'WAL mode allows readers and writers to proceed concurrently, unlike the rollback journal.\n\n' +
       'Subscribe to our newsletter.\n\n'*8)
_f = focus(_md, 'wal mode concurrent readers writers', chars=200)
assert 'concurrently' in _f and len(_f) <= 260, _f
assert 'concurrently' not in _md[:200]      # head truncation would have missed it
```

``` python
# a Cloudflare interstitial is a 200 that must NOT reach the corpus
class _P:
    def __init__(self, status=200, html=''): self.status, self.html_content, self.html = status, html, html
assert not usable(_P(200, '<html><head><title>Just a moment...</title></head><body>Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue</body></html>'))
assert not usable(_P(403, '<html>' + 'x'*500 + '</html>'))
assert not usable(None)
assert usable(_P(200, '<html><body>' + 'real prose about sqlite. '*40 + '</body></html>'))
assert _why(_P(429)) == 'http 429' and _why(None) == 'fetch failed'
```

``` python
# `usable` holds a page to `min_chars` of readable markdown; it used to ignore the argument.
_pg = _P(200, '<html><body>' + 'short prose about sqlite. '*40 + '</body></html>')
assert usable(_pg, min_chars=100) and usable(_pg, min_chars=0)
assert not usable(_pg, min_chars=5000)

# where and what-language are separate questions with separate answers
assert infer_country('rebuild my garage in australia') == 'au'
assert infer_country('garage rebuild sydney quotes') == 'au'           # cities count
assert infer_country('planning permission in the UK') == 'uk'
assert infer_country('compare australia and germany building codes') is None   # a comparison: neither
assert infer_country('garage rebuild cost') is None
assert infer_country('give us a quote') is None                        # bare 'us' is the pronoun
assert infer_country('australianism') is None                          # word boundaries

assert infer_language('what is the best way to do this for my house') == 'en'
assert infer_language('welche Vorschriften gelten für eine Garage in Österreich') == 'de'
assert infer_language('garage') is None                                # one word is not evidence
assert infer_language('la') is None                                    # shared across languages

# the join: country from the subject, language from the asker
assert infer_region('I want to rebuild my garage in australia, what is the regulation') == 'au-en'
assert infer_region('garage rebuild sydney') == 'au-en'
assert infer_region('do I need planning permission for a garage in the UK') == 'uk-en'
assert infer_region('what is the cost of living in france') == 'fr-en'  # French sources, English pages
assert infer_region('welche Vorschriften gelten für eine Garage in Österreich') == 'at-de'
assert infer_region('aktuelle KI Regulierung Österreich Unternehmen 2026') == 'at-de'  # no function words: fall to the country
assert infer_region('compare australia and germany building codes') == 'us-en'         # abstains to the default
assert infer_region('garage rebuild cost') == 'us-en'
assert infer_region('', dflt='au-en') == 'au-en' and infer_region(None) == 'us-en'
assert _region('garage in australia', 'uk-en') == 'uk-en'              # explicit beats inferred
```

``` python
# region and timelimit reach every backend: search() used to build the fused call without **kw,
# so `timelimit=` was accepted, ignored, and indistinguishable from having no effect.
_calls = []
def _spy(be, q, region='us-en', page=1, timeout=8, tries=2, **kw):
    _calls.append(dict(be=be, region=region, **kw))
    return [dict(title=be, href=f'https://e.com/{be}', body='', engine=be, rank=1)]
_real, _engine_hits = _engine_hits, _spy
try:
    search('sqlite wal mode', timelimit='y')
    assert [c['timelimit'] for c in _calls] == ['y']*len(TEXT_BACKENDS), _calls
    assert {c['region'] for c in _calls} == {'us-en'}

    _calls.clear(); search('rebuild my garage in australia')
    assert {c['region'] for c in _calls} == {'au-en'}, _calls
    assert not any('timelimit' in c for c in _calls)          # absent, not None: ddgs defaults it

    _calls.clear(); search('garage in australia', region='uk-en', timelimit='m', safesearch='off')
    assert {c['region'] for c in _calls} == {'uk-en'}
    assert all(c['timelimit'] == 'm' and c['safesearch'] == 'off' for c in _calls)

    _calls.clear(); assert search('  ') == [] and _calls == []   # empty query still touches no backend
finally: _engine_hits = _real
```

``` python
# a page's publication date, from the three places a page states it -- and None when it states none
class _D:
    def __init__(self, html='', url=''): self.html, self.url = html, url

_ld = lambda s: _D(f'<script type="application/ld+json">{s}</script>')
assert page_date(_ld('{"@type":"Article","datePublished":"2024-03-07T09:00:00Z"}')) == '2024-03-07'
assert page_date(_ld('{"@graph":[{"@type":"WebSite"},{"datePublished":"2019-11-02"}]}')) == '2019-11-02'
assert page_date(_ld('{"datePublished":"not a date","dateModified":"2024-05-05"}')) == '2024-05-05'
assert page_date(_D('<meta property="article:published_time" content="2022-06-15T10:11:12+00:00">')) == '2022-06-15'
assert page_date(_D('<meta name="DC.date.issued" content="2021-1-5">')) == '2021-01-05'      # zero-padded
assert page_date(_D('<meta name="viewport" content="width=1"><meta name="date" content="2025-12-31">')) == '2025-12-31'
assert page_date(_D('<time datetime="2023-08-01">last August</time>')) == '2023-08-01'
assert page_date(_D('', 'https://blog.example.com/2018/09/wal-mode')) == '2018-09-01'   # month only -> day 01
assert page_date(_D('<p>nothing dated here</p>', 'https://e.com/x')) is None            # undated stays undated

# a malformed JSON-LD block must not swallow the meta tag underneath it
assert page_date(_D('<script type="application/ld+json">{oops</script>'
                    '<meta name="pubdate" content="2020-02-29">')) == '2020-02-29'

# the month/day alternation has to prefer the longest branch, or 2019-11-02 reads as 2019-01-01
assert _iso('2019-11-02') == '2019-11-02' and _iso('2025-12-31') == '2025-12-31'
assert _iso('v1.2 build 7') is None
```
